searchText: The random sample on a huge validator set provides a minimal economic security sufficient for wallets and other low TVL features. I would never put funds a bridge _solely_ supported by the altair lightclient, but hybrid models do have value. I don't think making messages slash-able significantly increases the economic security of the feature. So basically: - low value consumers (wallets) use altair lc as is - high value consumers (bridges) wait for a full consensus zk circuit it would be interesting to understand the compute & data cost that you experienced in your implementation and see if we can come up with optimizations to bring them down to a level that would be acceptable One of the issues was computing the LC proof with respect to the parent of the head state, which requires keeping it around. Easy if you've got tree-states, but not so straightforward otherwise. <Phil_ngo> > <Phil_ngo> Hey @JuampiHernandez, tickets have already been released and sold out. Unfortunately due to venue constraints, a limited number of tickets were available. There will however be a recorded livestream for the talks and many of the light client contributors will be around throughout Devconnect and reachable through here. (re @JuampiHernandez: who can I talk with about tickets?)

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content:
The random sample on a huge validator set provides a minimal economic security sufficient for wallets and other low TVL features. I would never put funds a bridge _solely_ supported by the altair lightclient, but hybrid models do have value. I don't think making messages slash-able significantly increases the economic security of the feature. So basically:
- low value consumers (wallets) use altair lc as is
- high value consumers (bridges) wait for a full consensus zk circuit
